how: Made by hand on 2026-11-17, after G-3's Linux run at this commit, from another project's watcher's status file and period and from the host's journal, read after the run, with each time in UTC. A login the watcher's status file records is placed by that line; one computed from the period between two recorded lines is given with its bounds as start and end. A gate entry's case names the seed and run it fell in, as the gate's own table gives them, placed by the gate's step log, which gives each run's start and end; a fuzz entry's case names the target. Corrected on 2026-11-25: the backup run was first given as between runs of the gate's seeds; its first and last lines in the host's journal, 15:12:26Z and 15:12:29Z, both fall inside run 4 of 5 of run_length/bound-one-run-blocks, which the step log gives as 15:12:25Z to 15:12:32Z, and the journal does not show when the job's process ended.

not_listed.what: another project's watcher's remote logins, about every half hour from 2026-11-14T15:22:16Z, each reading the host's window state and a few files
not_listed.why: those that fell in the refused attempts of the kernel benchmark (four) and in the fuzz step that was no result (one) touch no committed file; the rest are listed as entries, each recorded time from the watcher's status file and each computed time with its bounds

not_listed.what: the host's own scheduled jobs: a repository backup every fifteen minutes, a health collector and two small watchers every five minutes, two sync jobs every ten minutes, a file backup about hourly and daily maintenance
not_listed.why: they run through every window and were not stopped, as nothing on the host is changed for a measurement beyond the governor; the run records keep no list of them by phase apart from the events listed here. What guards a figure differs by step. Each run of the bound-seed gate keeps the kernel's per-CPU counters copied before and after it, so each processor's busy share over the run and the processes started during it, the load read just before it began, and whether the process that kept the sibling cpu7 busy was running at its start and at its end; the gate passed a run only if it exited 0 with no finding, that process was running at both ends, and its time an execution was within the bar, and it held the busy shares, the load and the processes started to no rule. The timed fuzzing runs keep no per-CPU record and no load: each target's verdict is pass or fail by its own log, clean for its 1,800 s, and nothing guards a run's count of executions against a disturbance

not_listed.what: the host's scheduled repository backup's other runs inside this run's window: of the ten whose lines the host's journal holds from the bound-seed gate's start to the capacity check's end on 2026-11-17, the first is the entry listed here, and these are the other nine, each from its first to its last line in the journal, which does not show when the job's process ended. Seven fell in the fuzz step: 15:27:26Z to 15:27:27Z, before any timed run began, during fuzz_dictionary's and fuzz_pfor's replays and fuzz_itch_query's merge; 15:42:44Z to 15:42:45Z and 15:57:48Z to 15:57:51Z, in the timed runs of fuzz_itch_query, fuzz_dictionary and fuzz_pfor; 16:12:50Z to 16:12:52Z and 16:27:52Z to 16:27:53Z, in the timed runs of fuzz_itch_store, fuzz_run_length and fuzz_stream_vbyte; 16:43:01Z to 16:43:02Z and 16:58:18Z to 16:58:19Z, in fuzz_container's timed run. Two fell in the capacity check: 17:13:20Z to 17:13:22Z, in its ArcticDB part, and 17:28:38Z to 17:29:48Z, in its QuestDB class A part
not_listed.why: the one in the bound-seed gate is an entry: its first and last lines in the journal both fall inside one of the gate's timed runs, of about seven seconds, whose time against the bar is that run's figure. Each of these lasted seconds, the last about a minute, inside a step whose verdict is pass or fail by its own logs, and could only slow it: in a timed fuzzing run of 1,800 s it can take executions from the run, as a login can, and cannot hide a finding. They are listed here once, as the freeze's record lists the job's routine runs, and not as entries, so no mark and no table of runs shows them. The capacity check's file was measured at ede0176b10bb, so its two are listed in that commit's record too. The times are from the host's journal as read on 2026-11-25, after the run, which is not in the repository; the run's own records do not show them
